Counting that, s007 ('So why do the continents point south?') starts about 0:32 and ends about 0:38, the teaser stack runs to about 0:58, and real content (s010/s011 Bacon) starts about 1:01–1:04. Checklist A says end the first 30 s on the promise; the bench median for content start is 0:30, max 0:48.

issues.problem: Myth and refutation are out of order and point at the wrong thing. s005's 'You'd think Earth's spin did this ... called it just a coincidence' follows straight on from the two-thirds-of-land line. So 'It isn't. Not entirely.' reads as denying that the northern pile-up is coincidence, but s094 concludes it is 'a snapshot of where the drifting pieces happen to be'. That is the same idea as the Short's own 'we just happen to be alive when Earth happens to look like this' (pattern-26). Also, two refutations stacked in 8 s are both bare assertions: the spin myth isn't something viewers hold yet, and 'far too weak' (science-13 is about moving continents, not shaping them) is not shown. 'A video with tens of millions of views' reads like a citation or plug for another channel, against owner override 3.

Visual refutation for s006: the coin spins at {m:coin}, cracks on 'They're not', and on 'Not entirely' a 1.0-s unexplained flash shows South America, Africa and India sliding back to clamp around the yellow Antarctica ring, then snapping back to today. This is checklist B's 'flash the final reveal' and real evidence, not an assertion. Remove the SPIN FORCE gauge from s005. In s061, drop '(callback)' from the gauge note and delete the s005→s061 loop-ledger row; s061 works on its own.

That's a packaging overclaim that invites the 'Australia doesn't!' pile-on and breaks the owner's 'no false claims'. Title 6 'Earth Looks Like It's Melting' reads as climate change without the visual, so viewers who click expecting that are mismatched. Title 4 'It's NOT the Spin' plants a myth the hook can't prove by 1:00, and the spin line is now cut. 'Just Luck' is a vaguer opposite than 'coincidence', the word the hook and the 27M-view Short use. Title 2's 'Real Reason' promises a single cause that s093 refuses to give.

result.verdict: The visual plan is strong and mostly buildable. It has a clear house look, ten motivated Explorer gags, good callbacks (the tip-pop thump, the spin gauge, Bacon's page) and real data overlays. Measured against the engine it has five kinds of problem. (1) Some beats are physically impossible. The photoreal globe is opaque and orthographic, so a line cannot "pierce through the planet" (s008, s024, s029) and the globe cannot turn "semi-transparent" (s029, s044). All seven tips (s003) cannot be visible at once, and neither can a place and its antipode (s034, s107). Two globes with different overlays (s036) are impossible because the engine allows one overlay texture at a time. The continents cannot be packed into the Pacific honestly (s041), and the texture has no sea ice (s025). (2) Some assets are wrong or missing. assets/pd/bacon_p232.jpg is printed p.240 and does not contain 'acuminati'. I found the right pages: leaf n246 (p.239) has both 'acuminati' and 'non temere accidit', and leaf n387 (p.20) has the Parasceve repeat. green_fig1.jpg is a blank page; Figure 1 is green_n18.jpg. The only Cape of Good Hope sign photo on disk reads 'SCENIC WALK'. The Forster, Guyot, 1899, Ortelius, Humboldt and Wegener-1924 scans are not on disk. (3) Pacing. 73 of 109 segments have a gap of more than 5 s between marker-synced events, and the engine can only sync to {m:} markers. Two runs on the same globe last 74 s (4:33-5:47) and 66 s (9:40-10:46). (4) Some beats break the 2-element text limit: s055, s069, s072, s087, s097. (5) About 25 SFX names and a typewriter font are not in the library. The main structural fix is a new area-true Equal Earth flat-map mode, used for the tips (s002-s003, s021) and the antipode sequence (s033-s035). With it, plus waffle and 2x2-grid data cards, polar discs, profile panels and the cutaway drill, the video rotates through 9 modes and no segment asks for something the engine can't draw. Saved for builders: research/script/visual-director/asset_notes.json, plus the corrected Bacon pages in research/script/visual-director/dl_ia/ (n246.jpg, n387.jpg, box_n246.jpg, box_n387.jpg).

issues.problem: Monotony: about 54% of runtime is globe or paleo-globe, and the longest single-mode runs are 74 s (s033-s042, 4:33-5:47) and 66 s (s069-s078, 9:40-10:46). Both exceed the 20-40 s scene-change rule. There is also no flat-map mode at all, though several beats (s003, s033-s035) need everything visible at once.
issues.fix: Add an EQUAL EARTH FLAT MAP mode. Precompute it once in Python by inverse-projecting tex/day_8k.jpg (30% desat, navy ocean, faint graticule) and tex/data/antipodes.png at 3840 px wide. Place markers in JS with the forward formula: sin t = (sqrt3/2) sin phi; x = 2 sqrt3 lam cos t / (3(9A4t^8+7A3t^6+3A2t^2+A1)); y = A4t^9+A3t^7+A2t^3+A1t; A1=1.340264, A2=-0.081106, A3=0.000893, A4=0.003796. Use it in s003, s010, s021, s033-s035 and for the s086 tiles. Break the second long run with s069 (split diagram), s071 (black scrub card) and s074 (Bacon portrait cut). Planned mode mix: globe ~40%, paleo ~6%, flat map ~6%, archival ~13%, Explorer/3D ~11%, data cards ~10%, diagrams/cutaway ~9%, type cards ~5%.

issues.problem: The engine syncs events only to {m:} markers (api.T). By my estimate at 2.6 words/s, 73 segments have more than 5 s between marker-tied events (e.g. s056: 13.8 s; s089: 13.1 s; s095: 12.9 s; s057: 11.5 s; s097: 11.5 s). Unmarked beats written as 'on the word X' or 'then' cannot be timed.
issues.fix: Add a marker for every secondary event, at least one per 4 s of narration, without changing any words. Marker placements for the worst segments are in the rewrites (s005, s009, s010, s013, s017-s019, s024, s026, s029, s031-s032, s034-s035, s041, s043, s056, s069, s074, s090, s095). The same rule applies to s007 (add {m:answer} where Antarctica's ring flares), s023, s050, s057, s067, s070, s076, s078, s083, s087, s089, s092 and s104.

issues.problem: Text-count conflicts. Chapter cards (index + title) overlap each chapter-start segment's own on-screen text. The 'SIMPLIFIED' and 'MODEL' tags count as extra text elements (s072: card + SIMPLIFIED + years chip; s084: three).
issues.fix: Show chapter cards as a 2.0 s overlay on moving footage, finished before the segment's first pill. Merge the legal tags into the element they qualify: years chip 'MILLION YEARS AGO · SIMPLIFIED', pill '1970: THE REAL MAP (SIMPLIFIED)', 'MODEL: <NAME>'.

issues.problem: These SFX names are not in the engine library: coin flip, glass crack, camera shutter, zipper, boing, slide whistle, chalk squeak, door slam, drip plink, sizzle, pencil scratch, page turn, tape hiss, compass spin, bubbles, rock crack/grind, honey plop, film whir, bus horn, alarm ding, needle swish, audio logo. There is also no typewriter or handwriting font: F.FAM has no Special Elite.
issues.fix: Either generate a CC0 batch with these exact names or substitute from the library: page turn -> paper_rustle; rock crack -> impact_short + rumble_quake; alarm ding -> bell_small; camera shutter -> glitch_click; film whir -> time_rewind at -18 dB. For typewriter cards (s022, s023, s081) use JetBrains Mono 500 or add Special Elite (OFL) to www/fonts. Use Playfair Display 700i for the s058 letter.

issues.problem: Three.js stage time is about 95 s (gags, tetra, cutaway, card diorama, Kenney classroom), above the bench's 60 s guidance for software WebGL.
issues.fix: Pre-render with still.cjs every beat that only needs a still: the s039 grid, the s027 discs, the four model end-states (s009, s097, s104, s106, s107) and the s084 Gondwana still. Keep live stages for motion only.

issues.problem: 'Camera swings across the globe' to seven tips one event every 0.8 s does not fit the timing (8 words in about 3.4 s, so roughly 0.45 s per tip). The drip arrows are engine `arcs` from Cape Froward (-53.9,-71.3), Cape Agulhas (-34.8,20.0) and Kanyakumari (8.1,77.5) to (-78,20), with headDot. Full spec in rewrite.

issues.problem: 'The Arctic view color-inverts into the Antarctic one like a photo negative' doesn't work: a colour-inverted satellite image does not become Antarctica. The split-screen also needs two globe renders.
issues.fix: Use two 2D azimuthal equal-area discs built from ne_50m_land, two-tone (navy and cream). Invert the Arctic disc with a 'difference' composite so its colours swap and it visually rhymes with Antarctica. See rewrite.

issues.problem: The two poles are never visible together, so a drag from the Arctic to Antarctica needs a camera path. None is specified.
issues.fix: Drag the www/geo/arctic_ocean.geojson rings with `moves` along the 0° meridian over 2.5 s. The camera tracks the shape centroid at alt 2.6, starting at lat 70 and ending at lat -70 over Antarctica, outlined orange.

issues.problem: 'Globe turns semi-transparent' with an axis through the centre is impossible because the globe shader is opaque.
issues.fix: Show a 1.2 s cutaway drill from the North Pole to Antarctica, then a top-down Arctic view with Antarctica's outline mirrored onto it (lat→-lat, lon+180). The overlap with the Arctic Ocean fills yellow. See rewrite.

issues.problem: 'Flipped land slides away from real land like repelling magnets' misrepresents antipodes, which don't move.
issues.fix: Show a 1.0 s glimpse instead: tex/data/antipodes.png fades on and off over the globe (cyan with small yellow overlaps).

issues.problem: China and Kansas can't share a globe frame. The dig gag plus the cutaway need about 4.5 s, but only about 2.6 s remain between {m:dig} and {m:indian}. A 'progress bar' adds UI clutter.
issues.fix: Whip from China to the US on {m:test}, drop the Kansas marker on {m:kansas}, and set pause_after to 1.2. Then: dig gag (Explorer sinks into the planet), then a cutaway drill with no progress bar. See rewrite.

issues.problem: Where the Explorer 'tumbles out' is unspecified. The beat also puts three text elements on screen: INDIAN OCEAN, NEAREST LAND, and an Ile Saint-Paul label.
issues.fix: Rotate the tiny planet so the antipode (39.83S 81.42E) is on top and pop him out of the water. Then show the photoreal globe with a dashed line to Ile Saint-Paul (38.72S 77.53E) marked by a dot, not a label. The second pill replaces the first. See rewrite.

issues.problem: On a globe, Alaska's and Hawaii's antipodes fall near or past the limb from any view that also shows China.
issues.fix: Use the Equal Earth map. Draw all 50 states mirrored in cyan (lower 48 in the Indian Ocean, Hawaii on Botswana, Alaska's tip on Antarctica) and China in orange, then stamp.

issues.problem: China and Argentina are antipodes, so they are never visible together on a globe. 'Argentina lights orange and its flipped outline lands squarely on China' cannot be shown in one globe frame.
issues.fix: Use the Equal Earth map, with the Kenney mini composited onto it. Add markers {m:start} and {m:four}. See rewrite.

issues.problem: The three overlap pairs sit on opposite sides of the Earth, so a globe would need several rotations within 11 s. On the equirect texture the Antarctica/Arctic pair would look far too large (ledger caveat on numbers-21).
issues.fix: Use the Equal Earth map with a reprojected antipodes.png. Wipe in the cyan layer, then pulse the three yellow pairs in sequence, then the 1 IN 8 counter. See rewrite.

issues.problem: 'Side by side: left globe with continents scattered at random, right the real Earth' needs two globes with different overlays. The engine keeps one overlay texture at a time, and the random scatter is undefined.
issues.fix: Use a data card with two 10x10 waffle grids (29 vs 13 lit squares, no printed numbers). See rewrite.

issues.problem: 'Land inside it flickers brighter and dimmer as it searches' is vague.
issues.fix: Regenerate hemisphereCanvas each frame (1024x512 is enough) with a source-in composite against the land mask: land inside the cap glows orange and ocean inside it stays cyan. The cap centre sweeps along a scripted path that ends at 40N 2E, matching tex/data/stats.json.

issues.problem: Five dome jumps on the same globe extend one continuous globe run (s037-s040, about 35 s). Six red 'MOSTLY WATER' tags would be six text elements.
issues.fix: Use a 2x2... no: a 2x3 grid of pre-rendered hemisphere stills, each hit by a red X stamp icon. That's a mode change, with one headline pill. See rewrite.

issues.problem: All land is about 88% of the Pacific's area including marginal seas (148.9M vs 168.7M km²), and irregular rigid shapes can't be packed that tightly. So 'every continent dropped in at true size, with room to spare' would show overlaps or spill onto land: the image would be false. Seven thunks plus the Explorer gag also don't fit in 5.5 s.
issues.fix: Use an area-true 'pour', precomputed offline. Australia goes last, carrying the composited Explorer. Add markers {m:alone} and {m:room}, and set pause_after to 1.0. See rewrite.

issues.problem: 10.4 s with one event (the subscribe glow at 9.6 s).
issues.fix: At {m:taught}, a brand JUICE CHECK stamp spins in. At {m:checks}, it lands FALSE over the Kansas-antipode marker (callback). At {m:sub}, the button glows above the bottom 12%. See rewrite.

issues.problem: 'Tetrahedron wireframe rotates inside a translucent globe' isn't possible: tetraEarth's mesh is opaque.
issues.fix: Use tetraEarth at k=0 with edge opacity 0.9. The edges sit at 1.55R, so the four yellow corners poke out through the surface and the mid-edges dip inside, which reads as a pyramid hidden in the planet.

issues.problem: Green's title page is not on disk, and the minister line is tiny print.
issues.fix: Use archive.org vestigesmolteng00greegoog leaf n5 at w1600. Ken Burns 4x onto the line under 'WILLIAM LOWTHIAN GREEN' and crop out the Bodleian stamp and the handwritten shelfmark at the bottom.

issues.problem: assets/pd/green_fig1.jpg is a BLANK page, and the card-in-water diorama geometry is unspecified.
issues.fix: Figure 1 is assets/pd/green_n18.jpg (shield shape, N at top, point at S). Build the diorama from two 1.2x0.8 white planes hinged at 165° (a shallow roof), tilted 8° nose-down into a cyan water plane at 0.6 opacity. The dry part reads as a triangle aimed at the dipped end, with a white line along the analytic waterline. Fallback: underline 'by slightly arching a card' on preface leaf n7.

issues.problem: Two parts don't work. 'The face under the Explorer tilts': the top face is horizontal. 'Lands on a southern point': the south vertex is underneath the model, so he would be upside down.
issues.fix: Tilt the whole tetra group 25° toward camera while k ramps 0→1, so the top face slopes. He Rolls from the face centre (the North Pole) to the upper Americas vertex (19.47N, -75) and perches on that point (Idle_Neutral).

issues.problem: 'The tetrahedron rotates to show each feature as it's ticked' doesn't say which view goes with which tick.
issues.fix: Give each tick its own lookFrom. c1: side view, north up, three upper corners. c2: low side view along an edge running down to the south vertex. c3: view from straight above at the flat top face (Arctic). c4: view from straight below at the south vertex (Antarctica). c5: a vertex with the opposite face behind it.

issues.problem: The 1899 journal figure is not on disk, and a single Ken Burns runs 9.9 s with no event.
issues.fix: Fetch the Fig. 5 leaf from archive.org sim_geographical-journal_1899-03_13_3 and frame out the masthead (no citation look). Add {m:geo} on 'geographers' to underline 'tending to become tetrahedral', then cut to the rotating tetraEarth. Fallback: tetraEarth with a sepia grade and a '1899' pill. Do NOT substitute Green's 1875 figure.

issues.problem: 'The Explorer's Kansas tunnel line re-glows' doesn't work: the tunnel existed only in the cutaway stage, so on the globe there is nothing to re-glow.
issues.fix: Re-show the same yellow pulsing marker at 39.83S 81.42E inside the cyan mirrored North America outline, with the same sonar_ping.

issues.problem: The pin board with five labelled clues plus the headline puts six text elements on screen. Green's 'Figs. 7-10' aren't all on disk (green_globes.jpg = Figs 9-10).
issues.fix: Use five icon-only clue cards linked by red string to a tetrahedron icon with a red X, and use green_globes.jpg. See rewrite.

issues.problem: 14.8 s with one marker, at 13.8 s. The 'old-map texture' is unspecified, and the old maps on disk (Snider 1858, Hereford, Tabula Rogeriana) would misdate a pre-1620 beat.
issues.fix: Fetch Ortelius's 1570 Typus Orbis Terrarum (PD) and add markers {m:maps}, {m:mapmaker} and {m:stub}. See rewrite.

issues.problem: 11.5 s between the chapter card and {m:joined}.
issues.fix: Add {m:wrote} on 'wrote' (the portrait Ken Burns lands on the eyes, and an envelope icon slides in) and {m:fit} on 'fit' (the Atlantic coasts of both continents glow white before South America slides).

issues.problem: 'Every continent on the globe starts drifting slowly' invents motion: arbitrary drift directions misrepresent real plate motion.
issues.fix: Ken Burns on Wegener's own 1924 three-panel reconstruction map (PD; fetch from Commons category 'The Origin of Continents and Oceans - Wegener (1924)' and verify the figure). Fallback: a 3 s paleo scrub from 200 to 0 Ma. Then the smoke and a book stamped 1915 sinking.

issues.problem: The s066 'small marker on the ice sheet' implies a known find location that isn't in the ledger. s065 'desaturates' a photo that is already black and white. Which file is the departure photo is unverified: wegener_villumsen_1930.jpg's Commons caption is generic.
issues.fix: Fade s065 to pure white by ramping exposure over 3 s. In s066, show empty ice with snowfall and no marker. Before lock, check which asset (wegener_last_026.jpg or wegener_villumsen_1930.jpg) Commons captions as the Eismitte departure. On-screen text stays 'NOVEMBER 1930'.

issues.problem: 'AGENCY A / AGENCY B' labels plus the two pills make four text elements, and 'insets glare at each other' is vague.
issues.fix: Add {m:toe}. Slide a split diagram in from the right with a fingertip icon and a foot icon that tilt toward each other on record_scratch, and no labels. See rewrite.

issues.problem: Chapter card + SIMPLIFIED + years chip + title is over the text limit. 'Each piece glows as it's named' needs a mapping from polygons to continents that isn't specified.
issues.fix: Map polygon indices once from coast_000.json centroids and recolour per name with a PaleoOverlay colour function. Camera south-polar (lat -60, lon 20, alt 2.8). Years chip reads 'MILLION YEARS AGO · SIMPLIFIED'. See rewrite.

issues.problem: The paleo globe runs uninterrupted from 10:04 to about 11:12 (about 68 s). The Bacon callback is only a card over the same globe.
issues.fix: Cut away for 2.5 s to Bacon's portrait (assets/pd/bacon.jpg) with the question pill. Then the converging arrows use the real paleo tip positions from tracks.json. See rewrite.

issues.problem: The Explorer 'stands alone on Antarctica' while Gondwana breaks up, but tinyPlanet uses today's texture and can't show the breakup.
issues.fix: Composite the Explorer stage (transparent background, about 150 px) over the paleo globe at the projected south_pole track point, while T runs 140→60 Ma and the continents exit north. See rewrite.

issues.problem: The 'dotted ghost trails' are not specified as data.
issues.fix: Draw the real paths from paleo/tracks.json (cape_horn, cape_agulhas, kanyakumari, 0→180 Ma) as dotted yellow lines on the present-day globe, converging near Antarctica's ring. Add {m:apart} on 'drifted apart' to start the draw.

issues.problem: 'Continents morph into cartoon teardrops' implies point-correspondence morphing, which isn't built.
issues.fix: Fade in teardrop silhouettes, each sized to its continent's area and centred on its centroid with the point aimed south, over the dimmed continents (white outline draw-on, 0.6 s). In s085, those teardrop points extend into the s079 dotted tracks, which converge on Antarctica. That replaces the vague 'slide over the scar lines'.

issues.problem: The 12 tiles aren't listed, and 'base-to-tip' needs defined points.
issues.fix: South-pointing tiles: Baja, Florida, Greenland, Kamchatka, India, Malay Peninsula, Italy, Greece. North-pointing tiles: Cape York, Yucatán, Jutland, Taymyr. Each tile is a crop of the Equal Earth map with the peninsula orange. The needle runs from a hand-picked base point to the ledger tip coordinates (pattern-28/30); document those base points in the description.

issues.problem: Arrows 'all labelled N' would put up to eight text elements on screen.
issues.fix: Use unlabelled white arrows radiating from the South Pole, with the single pill 'EVERY DIRECTION: NORTH'.

issues.problem: No NASA astronaut photo of Baja is on disk.
issues.fix: Use the globe with tex/patch/baja.jpg. Baja's outline starts about 170 mi further south-east against mainland Mexico and slides north-west to today as the Gulf opens. See rewrite.

issues.problem: A 13.1 s gap between {m:fla} and {m:wafr}.
issues.fix: Add {m:reef} on 'reef platform' (the cross-section's pale limestone block rises under the peninsula and extends beyond its coast) and {m:creat} on 'tiny sea creatures' (a 1.5 s vector coral-polyp icon grows on the platform edge).

issues.problem: Run_Back is the wrong clip: to stay on top of a planet rolling about the view axis, the Explorer has to run sideways. The on-disk south-up and east-up medieval maps (tabula_rogeriana.jpg, hereford_mappa.jpg), which fit 'down is our invention', go unused.
issues.fix: Open on the Tabula Rogeriana rotating 180°, then the Blue Marble flip. For the gag, roll the planet about z while he plays Run facing screen-right. See rewrite.

issues.problem: The only sign photo on disk (Commons 'A sign board (Cape of Good Hope).jpg', saved at research/script/visual-director/dl_sign/sign.jpg) reads 'CAPE OF GOOD HOPE SCENIC WALK / KAAP DIE GOEIE HOOP WANDELPAD'. It does not show the 'most south-western' wording the narration quotes.
issues.fix: Download a CC photo whose legible text matches and verify it before narration lock. Otherwise cut the sign sentence and use the globe 'hop' fallback in the rewrite.

issues.problem: 'Small drips flicker each with its own icon' doesn't name the icons.
issues.fix: Baja: a tear-away arrow. Florida: a coral icon. Greenland: two diverging rift lines. All drawn as white line icons at the tips, about 0.6 s each.

issues.problem: cutawayEarth removes a quarter wedge, so it can't show two upwellings 180° apart (under Africa and under the Pacific).
issues.fix: Use a 2D equatorial slice with two plumes on opposite sides, a crossed-out north arrow and a Polaroid freeze. See rewrite.

issues.problem: At 19.1 s this is the longest segment, with a 12.9 s gap. The honey-spoon inset needs to be vector art (no footage).
issues.fix: Add six markers: DRIP callback, crumple, Nevada dive, cross-section, vector spoon in sync, quote. See rewrite.

issues.problem: 'Four empty panels each labelled MODEL' plus two pills makes six text elements. The engine also has no future-reconstruction data, so the panels' contents are undefined.
issues.fix: Use a 2x2 grid of pre-rendered stills with one header pill, naming each tile in s098-s101. Hand-key the model moves (see the s098 rewrite).

issues.problem: 'Our own redraw from Natural Earth polygons' gives no motion spec for any of the four models (s098-s101).
issues.fix: Hand-key true-size `moves` per model on a live globe shot, then save each end frame with still.cjs for the grid and filmstrip. See rewrite.

issues.problem: The heat-map overlay is unspecified.
issues.fix: Precompute a mask of the Proxima-style supercontinent's land and blur it inward so the interior is red (#FF5A36 to dark red) and the coastal fringes are cooler. Show it on the s098 still, labelled 'MODEL'. For the Explorer faint, use a tiny planet with a red key light and a subtle vertical sine-offset heat shimmer strip (no ctx.filter).

issues.problem: 'Half its words glow gold, half fade' has no defined meaning: which words?
issues.fix: Use a vertical split: big drips with gold Gondwana scars vs small drips grey with a '?'. Open on the n246 'non temere accidit' underline as the callback. See rewrite.

issues.problem: 'Frame after frame of drifting continents' doesn't say where the frames come from.
issues.fix: The filmstrip frames are real: paleo stills at 200, 150, 100 and 50 Ma, today, then the four model stills, scrolling left at a constant speed.

issues.problem: Four arrows from North America to Africa, Antarctica, Asia and Australia can't share one globe view.
issues.fix: Reuse the 2x2 model grid, ordered to match the spoken order, with each tile pulsing as it's named and a comment bubble at {m:oneword}. See rewrite.

issues.problem: The rift Y coordinates are not given.
issues.fix: Use three glowPaths from the Afar centre (11.5N 41.5E): Red Sea axis NW to 27N 34E; Gulf of Aden east to 12.5N 51E; East African Rift SSW to 4N 37E (this arm pulses). Fly-down: alt 3.0 to 0.35, tilt 0 to 40, over 3 s.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: (unchanged) Spin a globe, and Earth looks like it's {m:melt}melting.
VISUAL: Frame 1 = thumbnail in motion. globeShot keys {lat:-30, lon:20, alt:3.0, tilt:0, heading:0}, drift 2°/s. Look {desat:0.3, dim:0.35, ovAlpha:1}. Overlay: one fillEquirect canvas with South America, Africa and India in #FF5A36, glow 24. At {m:melt}, three `arcs` draw on, 1.0 s each, staggered 0.15 s: from Cape Froward (-53.9,-71.3), Cape Agulhas (-34.8,20.0) and Kanyakumari (8.1,77.5) to (-78,20), lift 0.08, white, headDot. A #FFD23F ring (F.dot ring) pulses on the South Pole with a 1.2 s period.
ONSCREEN: []
SFX: whoosh_soft at 0.0 (-12); shimmer under the arcs (-16).
rewrites.why: Gives builders exact values for the thumbnail match and keeps all three hero tips inside the limb (about 67° from centre).

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: (unchanged) {m:sam}South America, {m:afr}Africa, {m:ind}India. {m:grl}Greenland, {m:fla}Florida, {m:baja}Baja, {m:kam}Kamchatka.
VISUAL: No camera travel. At {m:sam}, {m:afr} and {m:ind}, in the s001 underside view, the named landmass flashes brighter while a white outline of its southern 15° draws on (strokeProjected, 0.35 s). Hard cut on {m:grl} (6-frame whoosh) to the EQUAL EARTH FLAT MAP, with SA, Africa and India already orange. Then each tip fills orange on its word: Greenland (Cape Farewell 59.8N 43.9W, admin-0); Florida (Cape Sable 25.3N 81.1W) and Baja (Cabo San Lucas 22.9N 109.9W), both from tips_admin1.geojson; Kamchatka (Cape Lopatka 50.9N 156.7E, tips_admin1). One pill at a time, each fading as the next pops.
ONSCREEN: ["GREENLAND","FLORIDA","BAJA","KAMCHATKA"] (one at a time; SA, Africa and India need no label)
SFX: pop_ui x7 (-14).
rewrites.why: Seven tips across more than 230° of longitude can't be whip-panned at 0.45 s each, and Kamchatka never shares a globe view with Greenland or Florida. The flat map shows all of them truthfully.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: Every point aims {m:south}south, like somebody left the planet {m:sun}out in the sun.
VISUAL: The flat map holds. At {m:south}, all seven tips get a short #FFD23F beats.dripArrow pointing straight down (len 70, staggered 0.06 s). At {m:sun}, hard cut to EXPLORER GAG 1 (planetGag, radius 3). The tiny planet is rotated so Cape Agulhas sits 20° in front of the top point, with a warm 2D sun flare in the top-right. An orange 3D teardrop (sphere + cone, 0.25 units) swells at the cape and slides down the planet's front curve. The Explorer Walks 0.4 s to the edge, then plays Interact (1.0 s) reaching down. The drop falls off the planet into space; he plays HitRecieve_2 (1.0 s), wobbling at the edge. Cut on the wobble into s004 (no Run_Back; there's no time).
ONSCREEN: []
SFX: cartoon_fall (-10).
rewrites.why: All seven tips can't glow at once on an orthographic globe. The gag needs a physical drop to 'catch', and it has to fit about 2.5 s.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: {m:twothirds}Two-thirds of all land sits north of the {m:eq}equator. So do nearly {m:nine}nine in ten people.
VISUAL: Globe {lat:15, lon:20, alt:3.2}. At {m:twothirds}, setOverlayURL('tex/data/land_north.png') fades in orange while look.dim rises to 0.45, darkening southern land. At {m:eq}, a glowing white equator line draws on (outline ring at lat 0, 1.0 s) and a split bar (barsShot, right third, above the bottom 12%) fills NORTH/SOUTH with F.counter rolling to 68%. At {m:nine}, the land overlay drops to 30%. White dots for every city in ne_110m_populated_places_simple pop in (radius proportional to sqrt(pop_max)), heavily northern, and the bar refills to about 88/12.
ONSCREEN: ["TWO-THIRDS OF ALL LAND: NORTH", "NEARLY 9 IN 10 PEOPLE: NORTH"] (sequential; the counter sits inside the bar)
SFX: tick_counter (-16).
rewrites.why: Replaces vague night-light dots with population data the engine already has (night lights track wealth, not people) and adds a mid-segment marker.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: You'd think Earth's {m:spin}spin did this. It's far {m:weak}too weak. A {m:vid}video with tens of millions of views called it {m:coin}just a coincidence.
VISUAL: At {m:spin}, the globe's heading spins 360° in 1.2 s (4-subframe motion blur) under curved white spin arrows, and small outward 'fling' arrows sprout from each continent. At {m:weak}, a 2D needle-dial gauge labelled SPIN FORCE (top-right) twitches and sags to near zero while the continents stay put. At {m:vid}, a generic white rounded play-button icon pops in centre-left (no channel name, no thumbnail). At {m:coin}, it flips edge-on into a spinning gold coin in front of the globe; the gauge fades out.
ONSCREEN: ["SPIN FORCE" (gauge label, gone before the quote), "\"JUST A COINCIDENCE\"?"]
SFX: whoosh_big on the spin; bell_small as a coin ring.
rewrites.why: Closes a 6.5 s dead gap in the cold open and gives the 'tens of millions of views' line a picture without using any Vsauce assets.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: Along the way: why you can't dig to China from {m:usa}anywhere in America. A half of the planet that's {m:water}eighty-nine percent water.
VISUAL: At {m:usa}, a 1.8 s hard cut to the cutawayEarth stage, with the shell rotated so Kansas (39.83N 98.58W) is on top (setFromUnitVectors(llDir(39.83,-98.58), up)). drillDir grows the cyan line from the top through the core and out the bottom in 1.2 s, and a yellow '?' pops at the exit. Camera st.lookFrom([6,3.5,6],[0,0.3,0],32). At {m:water}, cut to the globe centred (-40,-178), alt 2.8: a hemisphereCanvas cap fades in cyan and F.counter flashes 89% for 1.0 s.
ONSCREEN: ["89% WATER"]
SFX: sonar_ping on the drill; whoosh_soft.
rewrites.why: The photoreal globe is opaque, so no line can visibly punch through it. The cutaway drill is the engine's built-in tool for exactly this.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: A theory from {m:t1875}eighteen seventy-five that predicted all of it, and was {m:wrong}dead wrong. And {m:last}the last one: the continent your country is going to {m:crash}crash into. Eventually.
VISUAL: At {m:t1875}, a 0.8 s sepia flash of Green's Figure 5 (assets/pd/green_fig45.jpg, lower half), then the tetraEarth stage with k going 0→1 over 1.5 s (yellow edges). At {m:wrong}, it snaps back to a sphere (k 1→0, E.outBack) under a red X stamp. At {m:last}, cut to the cold-open globe spinning forward fast (heading +180°/s). At {m:crash}, a 1.0 s flash of the 2x2 grid of the four model end-state stills (pre-rendered from s098-s101), with the US white marker pulsing in each tile and one '?' in the centre. No single neighbour is shown. Hard cut to black on 'Eventually'.
ONSCREEN: ["1875", "MODELS"] (sequential)
SFX: impact_short on the X; impact_deep on the cut to black.
rewrites.why: Flashing one neighbour would spoil one model and contradict the four-way payoff in s102/s107. The new markers fill an 8.4 s gap.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: First, the {m:bad}bad news: you're not the first person to notice. {m:bacon}Not even close.
VISUAL: From black, fade up on the s003 flat map with the seven orange tips. At {m:bad}, a sepia paper wash wipes left to right across it (F.grade 'sepia', grain 10) while a year counter in the top-left (JetBrains Mono) rolls back from 2026 to 1620. At {m:bacon}, cross-dissolve to the 1620 Instauratio Magna title page (assets/pd/title_1620.jpg) in a rounded print frame. Ken Burns runs from the galleon (cx 0.5, cy 0.75, zoom 1.6) up to the title (0.5, 0.3, 1.15).
ONSCREEN: ["1620"] (the counter's landing value)
SFX: time_rewind (-12); paper_rustle.
rewrites.why: Removes the empty print frame (about 4 s) and turns the jump to 1620 into a visible time-travel move.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: In his Latin: {m:acum}acuminati. Sharpened to a point. And once wasn't enough; he wrote it {m:twice}twice, in the same book.
VISUAL: Use archive.org instauratiomagna00baco leaf n246 (printed p.239), saved at research/script/visual-director/dl_ia/n246.jpg. NOT assets/pd/bacon_p232.jpg, which is printed p.240 and lacks the word. Ken Burns from the full page into lines 4-6 ('Item Novus & Vetus Orbis ... versus Austrum autem angusti & acuminati'). At {m:acum}, a hand-drawn orange glowPath underline draws (0.4 s) under 'acuminati', normalized box x0.568 y0.229 w0.130 h0.022. At {m:twice}, the second page slides in from the right: leaf n387 (printed p.20, Parasceve), saved at dl_ia/n387.jpg, with an orange underline under 'ad Austrum angusta & veluti acuminata' (x0.154 y0.334 w0.517 h0.019). A red 'x2' stamp lands between the two pages.
ONSCREEN: ["\"ACUMINATI\": SHARPENED TO A POINT", "x2"]
SFX: glowPath pencil scratch (generate) or paper_rustle; stamp.
rewrites.why: The planned asset does not contain the word. These are the verified pages and pixel boxes.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: And in the very same {m:breath}breath, he said Africa and South America's matching capes were {m:accident}'not to be attributed to mere accident.'
VISUAL: From 0 to 2.3 s: globe (-25,-10, alt 2.6) with Africa and South America outlined white side by side and their southern capes pulsing orange. At {m:breath}, cut back to page n246 and tilt the Ken Burns UP two lines from 'acuminati': the 'not by accident' phrase is literally the sentence above, on the same 1620 page. At {m:accident}, orange underlines draw under 'quod non temere ac-' (x0.553 y0.131 w0.276 h0.017) and 'cidit.' (x0.079 y0.153 w0.064 h0.016), and the English pill fades in.
ONSCREEN: ["\"NOT TO BE ATTRIBUTED TO MERE ACCIDENT\""]
SFX: soft piano accent.
rewrites.why: Shows 'in the same breath' on the real page instead of a generic card, and adds a second event.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: So Bacon saw the drip, but couldn't {m:explain}explain it. For a very long time, neither could {m:anyone}anyone else. And boy, did they {m:try}try.
VISUAL: Page n246 shrinks into a print frame at the top-left over the slowly turning drip globe. At {m:explain}, a big '?' draws on Antarctica's yellow ring. At {m:anyone}, archival pages drop onto a stack, one every 1.1 s: Forster 1778 p.13 (fetch archive.org b30408623 page 13), Green 1875 preface (vestigesmolteng00greegoog leaf n7) and Guyot 1849 p.22 (fetch earthmanlectures00guyo page 22). At {m:try}, the stack topples sideways off-frame.
ONSCREEN: []
SFX: paper_rustle x3; whoosh_soft on the topple.
rewrites.why: A 9.1 s segment had zero markers and relied on scans that aren't on disk. Somerville, who is never named, is dropped.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: Captain {m:cook}Cook's naturalist, Johann Reinhold Forster, noticed that every great southern tip looks {m:alike}alike: high, rocky, the end of a {m:mtn}mountain chain.
VISUAL: From 0 to 2.6 s: Ken Burns on assets/pd/forster.png (Bause after Graff) in a sepia print frame. At {m:alike}, cut to the globe with relief 1.0 and patch tex/patch/s_america_tip.jpg: camera low over Cape Froward looking north up the Andes {lat:-52, lon:-72, alt:0.25, tilt:55, heading:0}. At {m:mtn}, whip to Kanyakumari with patch s_india.jpg, tilt 55, looking north up the Western Ghats. Draw no 'chain' lines from Cape Agulhas or Tasmania.
ONSCREEN: ["\"A GREAT AND STRIKING SIMILARITY\""]
SFX: whoosh_soft on the whip.
rewrites.why: Cape Agulhas has no north-running chain, so drawing one would endorse a wrong generalisation. The real terrain makes the same point honestly.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: His explanation? A giant flood came {m:wave}roaring in from the south-west and carved every one of them. Some of the top scientists of the day {m:bought}bought it. Geology {m:didnot}did not.
VISUAL: EXPLORER GAG 2 (planetGag, South Atlantic facing camera). At {m:wave}, a 2D stylised wave (flat cyan crest with a white foam line) sweeps across the frame from lower-left (south-west) to upper-right over 1.4 s. The Explorer plays Run_Right 1.0 s ahead of it, then Roll as the crest passes over him, ending flat on his back (Idle_Neutral). At {m:bought}, cut to the fetched Forster 1778 p.13 scan with an orange underline under 'a violent flood coming from the south-west'. At {m:didnot}, a small wave icon in the page margin deflates (scaleY 1→0.1, 0.4 s).
ONSCREEN: ["FORSTER'S CAUSE: \"A VIOLENT FLOOD\""]
SFX: whoosh_big; splash_big; deflate pfft (generate).
rewrites.why: Texture tips can't 'sharpen'. The new markers cover a 9.6 s gap.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: Because the shapes are only clue {m:one}number one. Clue number two is on the {m:far}far side of the planet.
VISUAL: At {m:one}, the seven drip arrows from s003 flash once on the cold-open globe while the camera pushes in. At {m:far}, hard cut to the cutawayEarth stage with the North Pole on top. drillDir draws the cyan line from the pole through the core and out the South Pole in 1.4 s while the camera dollies in, st.lookFrom from [6,3.5,6] to [4.5,2.6,4.5], target [0,0.3,0], fov 32.
ONSCREEN: []
SFX: riser_tension (start 4 s early); sonar_ping.
rewrites.why: A line through the planet can only be shown on the cutaway, not on the opaque globe.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: Start at the very top of the world. The {m:np}North Pole isn't land. It's ocean. Stand on the ice there, and the sea floor is about {m:depth}two and a half miles beneath your boots.
VISUAL: Chapter card as a 2 s F.chapterCard overlay on moving footage. The camera flies to {lat:85, lon:0, alt:1.4, tilt:35}, showing the dark bathymetric Arctic basin ringed by land (the texture has no sea ice). At {m:np}, a pulsing white marker labelled NORTH POLE. At {m:depth}, cut to a 2D PROFILE PANEL: a vertical slice from Greenland across the pole to Siberia, with a thin white sea-ice line at the surface, navy water and the sea floor 2.5 mi down. A depth ruler drops from the ice to the floor (tick_counter), and a small pre-rendered Explorer sprite stands on the ice line.
ONSCREEN: ["WHAT'S ON EARTH'S OTHER SIDE?" (card), "SEA FLOOR: ~2.5 MILES DOWN"]
SFX: sonar_ping; rumble under the ruler.
rewrites.why: Removes sea ice the texture doesn't have and the impossible 'globe slices open'. Introduces a profile-diagram mode.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: Now go to the {m:bottom}bottom. At the {m:sp}South Pole, you're standing almost {m:up}two miles up, on a sheet of ice more than a mile and a half thick.
VISUAL: At {m:bottom}, the profile panel whips down to a South Pole profile on the same axis scale: a dashed sea-level line, rock below, a white ice sheet above. At {m:sp}, a marker labelled SOUTH POLE. At {m:up}, the ice column grows to almost 2 miles with an upward ruler, and on 'a mile and a half thick' a bracket draws along the ice. The Explorer sprite stands on top shivering (Idle). It's a gag, not a scale reference.
ONSCREEN: ["SOUTH POLE: ~2 MILES UP"]
SFX: ice_wind.
rewrites.why: Fills an 8.5 s gap and drops the false 'for scale' claim.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: The two ends of the planet are {m:neg}photographic negatives. Ocean on top. A continent at the bottom.
VISUAL: Two 2D POLAR DISCS, each 520 px, azimuthal equal-area from ne_50m_land (Antarctica includes ice shelves), slowly counter-rotating. Left: Arctic, with a navy ocean centre and a cream ring of land. Right: Antarctica, with a cream land centre and a navy ring of ocean. At {m:neg}, the Arctic disc inverts via a 'difference' composite against white (cream and navy swap over 0.4 s), and its cream centre now rhymes with the Antarctic disc.
ONSCREEN: ["OCEAN ON TOP. LAND AT BOTTOM."]
SFX: glitch_click (as a shutter).
rewrites.why: A colour-inverted satellite image can't 'become' Antarctica. Two-tone discs make the negative idea literal and cost one cheap 2D render.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: But here's the part that doesn't make sense. They don't just match. They {m:line}line up. Most of {m:ant}Antarctica sits directly opposite the Arctic Ocean, on the exact {m:other}other side of the Earth.
VISUAL: Music cuts 0.5 s before {m:line}. At {m:line}, cut to the cutawayEarth stage (North Pole on top) as drillDir shoots from the pole through the core into Antarctica in 1.2 s, with a bass hit. At {m:ant}, cut to the globe looking straight down on the Arctic {lat:90, alt:2.4}. www/geo/arctic_ocean.geojson is outlined cyan, and Antarctica's outline mirrored to its antipode (lat→-lat, lon→lon+180) draws on in orange. At {m:other}, the intersection of mirrored Antarctica and the Arctic Ocean fills yellow.
ONSCREEN: ["MOST OF ANTARCTICA <-> ARCTIC OCEAN"]
SFX: impact_deep at {m:line}.
rewrites.why: The globe can't turn semi-transparent. This shows the axis on the cutaway and the overlap on real polygons.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: If you dig straight down, you'll reach {m:china}China. Let's {m:test}test it. Start in {m:kansas}Kansas, right at the center of the lower forty-eight, and {m:dig}dig. [pause_after 1.2]
VISUAL: At {m:china}, the globe is centred on China (35N 105E, alt 2.6) and China fills orange. At {m:test}, whip west to the US (39N 98W): China is on the far side and can't share the frame. At {m:kansas}, a marker drops at 39.83N 98.58W with a pill. At {m:dig}, EXPLORER GAG 3a (planetGag, Kansas rotated to the top): Interact loops as a digging motion with 2D dirt puffs, and moveAlong lowers him 0.6 units into the planet over 1.2 s until he disappears. Then, during the pause, cut to cutawayEarth with Kansas on top: drillDir runs from Kansas through the core in 1.4 s. No progress bar.
ONSCREEN: ["KANSAS"]
SFX: dig_shovel; sonar_ping.
rewrites.why: China and Kansas can't share a globe frame, and the dig gag plus drill needed about 2 s more than the draft allowed.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: You come out in the {m:indian}southern Indian Ocean. The {m:nearest}nearest land is a tiny French island, more than two hundred miles away.
VISUAL: The drill line exits at the bottom of the cutaway. At {m:indian}, cut to the tiny planet rotated so 39.83S 81.42E (Kansas's antipode) is on top, all blue. The Explorer shoots up out of the water (moveAlong y from -0.6 to +0.4), plays Roll, then Idle waist-deep inside a 2D ripple ring. At {m:nearest}, cut to the photoreal globe over the antipode {alt:0.35, tilt:40}: a yellow pulsing marker sits at 39.83S 81.42E, a dashed great-circle line draws on to Ile Saint-Paul (38.72S 77.53E), and the island is a tiny white dot with no label.
ONSCREEN: ["INDIAN OCEAN" → replaced at {m:nearest} by "200+ MILES TO THE NEAREST LAND"]
SFX: splash_big.
rewrites.why: Pins down a location the draft left vague and keeps text to two elements.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: Even if you {m:start}started in China, three times out of {m:four}four you'd surface in the ocean. The people who can actually dig to China? {m:arg}Argentinians.
VISUAL: EQUAL EARTH MAP, where a place and its antipode are both on screen. At {m:start}, China's antipodal outline (cyan) draws on over the South Pacific and South Atlantic off Chile and Argentina. At {m:four}, the part over water fills cyan and the sliver over Argentina and Chile fills yellow (about a quarter). At {m:arg}, Argentina fills orange and its own antipodal outline draws on in cyan right on top of China, with the overlap in yellow. A Kenney mini (mini_male_a, separate stage with transparent background, about 110 px) pops up on Argentina and plays emote-yes.
ONSCREEN: ["ARGENTINA -> CHINA"]
SFX: ding (bell_small).
rewrites.why: Antipodes are never visible together on a globe, so the flat map is required.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: Now flip {m:flipall}every continent to the far side of the planet and lay it over the {m:orig}original. Only about {m:eighth}one-eighth of the land has land on the other side.
VISUAL: EQUAL EARTH MAP (area-true, so the Antarctica/Arctic pair isn't inflated). At {m:flipall}, the reprojected antipodes.png cyan layer wipes in left to right over grey real land. At {m:orig}, the yellow overlaps pulse one at a time with a chime: South America with East Asia, then Antarctica with the Arctic, then New Zealand with Spain (with a 1.5x Ken Burns punch-in). At {m:eighth}, the hero counter shows 1 IN 8.
ONSCREEN: ["ONLY ABOUT 1 IN 8"]
SFX: shimmer x3; tick_counter.
rewrites.why: Shows all three pairs in one frame, honestly sized, and adds a mid-segment marker.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: That's less than half of what you'd expect if the continents had been {m:random}sprinkled at random.
VISUAL: DATA CARD on navy with two 10x10 waffle grids of land squares. Left grid: IF RANDOM. Right grid: REAL EARTH. At {m:random}, squares light yellow (land with land opposite) in a fast random order; the left stops at 29 and the right at 13. A white bracket shows the right is under half. No numbers are printed (hero-number rule); the grids carry the ratio.
ONSCREEN: ["IF RANDOM", "REAL EARTH"]
SFX: tick_counter.
rewrites.why: Two globes with different overlays can't render together (one overlay texture), and the random scatter was undefined. This also breaks the 74 s globe run.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: (unchanged) There is no way to cut this planet in half and get a half that's mostly land.
VISUAL: Mode change to a 2x3 grid of pre-rendered globe stills (still.cjs). Each still shows a hemisphere cap centred on Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica and Australia respectively (ocean inside the cap cyan, land inside it orange). A red X stamp icon (no words) slams onto each tile in turn, 1.0 s apart. The tiles drift slightly so nothing is static.
ONSCREEN: ["NO HALF IS MOSTLY LAND"]
SFX: stamp x6 (-16).
rewrites.why: Breaks a roughly 35 s single-globe run, and six worded tags would break the text limit.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: The Pacific {m:alone}alone could swallow {m:drop}every continent on Earth, with {m:room}room to spare. [pause_after 1.0]
VISUAL: Globe centred on the Pacific {lat:-5, lon:-160, alt:2.6}. At {m:alone}, the Pacific (NE 10m marine polygons including its marginal seas) is outlined cyan. From {m:drop}, the continents lift off as orange shapes (moves, 0.5 s apart, overlapping). As each reaches the Pacific it 'melts' into an orange pour that spreads outward from the basin centre. The pour is an area-true raster computed offline: Pacific cells ordered by distance from the centre, filled until the filled area equals the land dropped so far. Australia comes last carrying the Explorer (stage render composited at the shape's projected centroid, about 140 px tall). At {m:room}, the pour stops, leaving a blue rim. The Explorer plays Idle_Neutral looking around, then Wave.
ONSCREEN: ["PACIFIC > ALL LAND COMBINED"]
SFX: thunk_heavy per landing (-14).
rewrites.why: Land is about 88% of the Pacific's area, so rigid true-size continents can't be packed in without overlapping. The pour is honest, and the Pacific drop still works as a Short.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: Every week, Myth Juice takes {m:taught}one thing you were taught about the world and {m:checks}checks it against the map. If you want the next one, {m:sub}subscribe.
VISUAL: A slow orbit of the globe with the antipode overlay glowing; the picture never freezes. At {m:taught}, the brand JUICE CHECK stamp spins in at the upper left. At {m:checks}, it lands as FALSE with a thud over the yellow Kansas-antipode marker in the Indian Ocean (callback). At {m:sub}, an animated subscribe button glows in the lower third, above the bottom 12%.
ONSCREEN: ["JUICE CHECK: FALSE", "SUBSCRIBE"]
SFX: stamp; pop_ui.
rewrites.why: Before this, 10.4 s had one event. Now the subscribe ask also repeats the brand verdict device.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: His big idea: the Earth was cooling, shrinking, and slowly collapsing toward a {m:tet}tetrahedron. A four-cornered {m:pyr4}pyramid.
VISUAL: tetraEarth stage (radius 2.2). The Explorer stands on top, where the North Pole is the centre of the future top face. At {m:tet}, k ramps from 0 to 1 over 3 s while the whole group tilts 25° toward camera so the top face slopes. The Explorer plays Roll along moveAlong from the face centre to the near upper corner (19.47N, -75, the Americas vertex). At {m:pyr4}, he stops perched on that point (Idle_Neutral) and the yellow edges flare.
ONSCREEN: ["EARTH BECOMING A TETRAHEDRON"]
SFX: slide whistle (generate) or cartoon_fall (-12).
rewrites.why: The top face never tilts on its own, and the south vertex is underneath the model, so he can't land there without standing upside down.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: The pyramid quietly vanished from geology. Green's checklist was {m:real}real. He'd just pinned the clues on the wrong {m:suspect}suspect.
VISUAL: Green's globe engravings (assets/pd/green_globes.jpg, Figs 9-10) drift away in sepia. At {m:real}, five icon-only clue cards appear on a dark board: an ocean cap, Antarctica, a south-pointing triangle, a north-heavy globe, and an antipode double-arrow. At {m:suspect}, red strings link all five to a tetrahedron icon, which gets a red X.
ONSCREEN: ["REAL CLUES. WRONG SUSPECT."]
SFX: pin stab (generate) or impact_short (-14).
rewrites.why: Five worded clue labels plus the headline would be six text elements, and Figs 7-8 aren't on disk.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: The real culprit had been staring out of {m:maps}world maps for centuries. A {m:mapmaker}mapmaker had floated it even before Bacon wrote his line. It just needed someone {m:stub}stubborn enough to say it out loud: the continents {m:move}move.
VISUAL: At {m:maps}, Ken Burns across Ortelius's 1570 Typus Orbis Terrarum (PD; fetch from Commons), pushing in on the Atlantic. At {m:mapmaker}, orange glowPaths trace the facing coasts of South America and Africa on the old map, and the '1596' pill appears. At {m:stub}, cross-dissolve to the photoreal globe {lat:-10, lon:-15, alt:2.4} with the same two coasts glowing. At {m:move}, South America and Africa twitch apart 0.3° (moves, 0.2 s).
ONSCREEN: ["1596: THE AMERICAS \"TORN AWAY\""]
SFX: paper_rustle; rumble_quake (-12) at {m:move}.
rewrites.why: A 14.8 s segment had one marker, and the on-disk old maps (Snider 1858, Hereford, Tabula Rogeriana) would misdate the beat.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: Today, satellites clock the continents moving at about the speed your {m:nail}fingernails grow. Or your {m:toe}toenails, depending on which government agency you ask.
VISUAL: Globe on the Atlantic. White GPS-style velocity arrows appear on the plates. At {m:nail}, a split diagram slides in from the right (mode change): a vector fingertip whose nail edge creeps forward. At {m:toe}, a vector foot icon slides in beside it, and the two icons tilt toward each other as if arguing. No AGENCY labels.
ONSCREEN: ["PLATE SPEED = FINGERNAIL GROWTH", "OR TOENAILS?"]
SFX: record_scratch (-14) on 'agency'.
rewrites.why: The AGENCY A/B labels made four text elements, and 'glare' had no drawable meaning. This also breaks the 66 s globe run.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: Rewind into the age of dinosaurs, and watch the southern continents slide home: {m:r_sam}South America, {m:r_afr}Africa, {m:r_ind}India, {m:r_aus}Australia.
VISUAL: Chapter card as a 2 s overlay. Then the paleo globe (PaleoOverlay, look {flatBase:1, ovAlpha:1, ovMul:1, nightAmt:0, relief:0}) from a south-polar camera {lat:-60, lon:20, alt:2.8} so Gondwana assembles centre-frame. T scrubs from 0 to 180 Ma across the segment (E.inOut). Map paleo polygon indices to continents once, using coast_000.json centroids. At each name marker, that continent's polygons fill orange through a per-polygon colour function.
ONSCREEN: ["WHERE ARE THE DRIPS POINTING?" (card), years chip labelled "MILLION YEARS AGO · SIMPLIFIED"]
SFX: time_rewind.
rewrites.why: Fixes the text count, and the 'glows as named' beat needed a polygon-to-continent mapping.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: {m:remember}Remember Bacon's open question? Is there even a southern continent? The drips were {m:point}pointing at it {m:whole}the whole time.
VISUAL: At {m:remember}, cut for 2.5 s to Bacon's portrait (assets/pd/bacon.jpg, sepia, Ken Burns toward the eyes) with the question pill. At {m:point}, cut back to the assembled Gondwana paleo globe. At {m:whole}, white dripArrows run from the 180 Ma positions of Cape Horn, Cape Agulhas and Kanyakumari (from paleo/tracks.json) and converge on the yellow ring at the south_pole track point.
ONSCREEN: ["\"WHETHER THERE IS ANY SOUTHERN CONTINENT\""]
SFX: single piano note; music cut 0.5 s before {m:whole}.
rewrites.why: The cut to Bacon's portrait breaks a roughly 68 s run of the paleo globe, and the arrows now use real reconstructed positions.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: And then everyone {m:leave}leaves. Except {m:stay}Antarctica. It barely moves.
VISUAL: T runs from 140 to 60 Ma. Africa, South America, India and Australia drift north out of frame while Antarctica stays centred. EXPLORER GAG 8: the Explorer stage (transparent background) is composited over the paleo globe at the projected south_pole track point, about 150 px tall. At {m:leave}, he plays Wave toward the departing continents. At {m:stay}, Antarctica's yellow ring pulses beneath him.
ONSCREEN: ["ANTARCTICA STAYS PUT"]
SFX: whoosh_soft as each continent exits.
rewrites.why: tinyPlanet uses today's texture and can't show Gondwana breaking up, so the Explorer has to be composited onto the paleo globe.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: Some smaller drips have stories all their own. Several million years ago, the Pacific Plate grabbed {m:baja}Baja and started dragging it away from Mexico. It's still {m:going}going.
VISUAL: Globe with patch tex/patch/baja.jpg {lat:27, lon:-112, alt:0.35, tilt:45}. At {m:baja}, Baja (tips_admin1: Baja California + Baja California Sur) is outlined orange, first shown pushed about 170 mi south-east against mainland Mexico (moveRings offset). It then slides north-west to its present position over 2.5 s as the Gulf of California opens behind it, with a white Pacific Plate arrow pointing NW. At {m:going}, the arrow keeps pulsing.
ONSCREEN: ["BAJA: TORN AWAY FROM MEXICO"]
SFX: rumble_quake (-14).
rewrites.why: There's no NASA Baja photo on disk. This beat uses data the engine has and actually shows the motion.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: Even {m:down}'down' is our own invention. The most famous photo of Earth ever taken was shot with {m:bm}Antarctica on top. It got {m:flipped}flipped, because that's how we're used to seeing it.
VISUAL: At {m:down}, Ken Burns on al-Idrisi's south-up Tabula Rogeriana (assets/pd/tabula_rogeriana.jpg, on disk and unused so far), rotating 180° so the Mediterranean snaps into its familiar shape. At {m:bm}, assets/pd/bluemarble_original.jpg (south-up) fills the frame. At {m:flipped}, it rotates 180° and dissolves into bluemarble_northup.jpg. EXPLORER GAG 9 (last 3 s): the tiny planet rolls 180° about the camera axis (planet.rotation.z) while the Explorer plays Run facing screen-right and stays on top like a hamster in a wheel. He ends in Idle_Neutral, upright on the now south-up planet.
ONSCREEN: ["1154: SOUTH WAS UP", "SHOT WITH ANTARCTICA ON TOP"] (sequential)
SFX: whoosh_soft on each rotation.
rewrites.why: Run_Back is the wrong clip for a roll about the view axis. The south-up medieval map on disk illustrates 'down is our invention'.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT (fallback unless a verified sign photo is found): And Africa's southern tip isn't even the {m:gh}Cape of Good {m:hope2}Hope.
VISUAL: Globe over the Cape {lat:-34.5, lon:19.2, alt:0.25, tilt:40} with patch s_africa.jpg. At {m:gh}, a white marker pulses on the Cape of Good Hope (34.36S 18.48E). At {m:hope2}, a dashed line hops about 90 mi east-south-east to Cape Agulhas (34.83S 20.0E), and a thin latitude line shows Agulhas sits farther south. If a CC photo whose legible text reads 'most south-western point' is downloaded and checked, restore the original sentence and Ken Burns onto that sign text. The on-disk sign.jpg ('SCENIC WALK') must not be used.
ONSCREEN: ["REAL TIP: CAPE AGULHAS"]
SFX: comic sting (bell_small).
rewrites.why: The only sign photo on disk doesn't show the quoted wording, so the beat can't be built as written.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: As for all that land piled up in the north, there's no clear sign of a deep {m:force}force dragging it there. Most likely, it's a {m:snap}snapshot of where the drifting pieces happen to be right now.
VISUAL: A 2D EQUATORIAL SLICE: a full Earth disc with crust, mantle and core rings, and two broad orange plumes rising on opposite sides. Small continent silhouettes on the rim (Africa on one side, Pacific islands on the other) do the labelling, with no text. At {m:force}, a grey arrow pointing north fades in over the disc and gets a red X. At {m:snap}, a white flash freezes the s001 drip globe inside a white Polaroid border.
ONSCREEN: ["NOT A FORCE. A SNAPSHOT."]
SFX: glitch_click (shutter).
rewrites.why: The cutaway wedge can't show two upwellings 180° apart, and the new marker fills a 9.6 s gap.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: And here's one more {m:irony}irony. 'Continental drip' started as a {m:joke2}joke, but geologists have since found {m:realdrip}real drips. Under {m:nev}Nevada, a cold blob of rock is sinking into the Earth like {m:honey}honey off a spoon. The scientist who found it admitted he'd been {m:anti}'anti-drip' since his early days.
VISUAL: At {m:irony}, a 1.5 s callback to the 1973 typewriter sheet (DRIFT→DRIP). At {m:joke2}, the sheet crumples (scale and rotate) and drops out of frame. At {m:realdrip}, the globe dives to Nevada {lat:39, lon:-117, alt:0.4} with a pulsing marker. At {m:nev}, cut to a 2D cross-section under the western US: crust and mantle, with a cold blue blob and long tail stretching downward over 4 s (bezier, 60 mi wide by 300+ mi deep in proportion). At {m:honey}, a vector spoon inset (top-right) drips amber honey in the same shape, in sync. At {m:anti}, the quote pill pops.
ONSCREEN: ["REAL DRIP: UNDER NEVADA (SIMPLIFIED)", "\"ANTI-DRIP\""]
SFX: typewriter; paper crumple (paper_rustle); honey plop (generate).
rewrites.why: At 19.1 s this is the longest segment and it had one marker. It now has an event roughly every 3 s.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: Give it a couple hundred million years, and geologists think a new supercontinent will {m:form}form. They just can't agree on what it looks like. So here are the four main {m:models}models.
VISUAL: A time-scrub bar runs forward past TODAY. At {m:form}, the globe spins forward fast and fogs over. At {m:models}, four tiles slide in as a 2x2 grid. Each is a pre-rendered still of today's globe centred on North America with the white US tracked marker. The tiles stay unnamed until s098-s101 name them one by one.
ONSCREEN: ["4 MODELS, 200-250 MILLION YEARS OUT"]
SFX: riser_tension.
rewrites.why: Four MODEL labels plus two pills would be six text elements, and the new marker fills an 11.5 s gap.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: (unchanged) One: the Atlantic {m:prox}slams shut, and America crashes back into Africa in about two hundred fifty million years. Pangaea Proxima.
VISUAL: Tile 1 expands into a live globe shot {lat:25, lon:-30, alt:2.4}. The engine has no future-reconstruction data, so each model is hand-keyed true-size `moves` of Natural Earth continents, about 3 s each, eased. Proxima: North America moves east and rotates about 20° to close against north-west Africa and Iberia, and South America moves east to close against West Africa. The US white marker rides North America and bumps into Africa at {m:prox}. Hold 1 s, then save this end frame with still.cjs for the grid and filmstrip. Same template for the others. s099 Novopangaea: camera on the Pacific; the Americas move west and Antarctica moves north into the gap. s100 Amasia: camera over the North Pole; North America rotates north over the pole onto Siberia. s101 Aurica: camera on the Pacific; the Americas move west while Asia and Australia move east, leaving Australia at the centre.
ONSCREEN: ["MODEL: PANGAEA PROXIMA"]
SFX: thunk_heavy.
rewrites.why: 'Our own redraw' was unspecified. This gives a buildable recipe for all four models and the stills used in s009, s097, s104, s106 and s107.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: Four hundred years ago, Bacon said the likeness of Africa and South America wasn't an {m:acc2}accident. He was {m:half}half right. And nobody knows yet which future {m:wins}wins.
VISUAL: At {m:acc2}, page n246 returns with 'quod non temere accidit' underlined in orange (callback to s013). At {m:half}, the frame splits vertically. Left: the drip globe with the three Gondwana scar lines glowing gold (the big drips were no accident). Right: the small drips (Baja, Florida, Greenland, Kamchatka) flickering grey with a '?' (no single answer). At {m:wins}, the 2x2 model grid flashes behind the '?'.
ONSCREEN: ["HALF RIGHT"]
SFX: piano note.
rewrites.why: 'Half its words glow gold' had no defined meaning. The split shows exactly which half Bacon got right.

rewrites.new_text:
TEXT: (unchanged) So which neighbor are you betting on? Africa, Antarctica, Asia or Australia. {m:oneword}One word, in the comments.
VISUAL: The 2x2 grid of model end-state stills, ordered to match the spoken order: Africa = Proxima, Antarctica = Novopangaea, Asia = Amasia, Australia = Aurica. Each tile pulses with a coloured border as its neighbour is named. At {m:oneword}, a comment-bubble icon pops over the centre.
ONSCREEN: ["ONE WORD: WHICH NEIGHBOR?"]
SFX: pop_ui.
rewrites.why: Arrows from North America to all four candidates can't share one globe view. The grid reuses the stills that are already planned.

title_options: Why the Continents Point South (Not Just a Coincidence)
Earth Looks Like It's Dripping. Your Map Never Said Why
The Continents Are Pointing at Something
A 400-Year-Old Clue in the Shape of the Continents
Why Every Map Looks Like It's Dripping South
Why Earth Drips South, and Where It's Dripping Next
thumbnail_concepts: CAN'T UNSEE IT (UNSEE in pure red #FF2B2B, not the #FF5A36 land hue; white text on black boxes, top-left). Built from the EXACT frame-1 render (s001: same ~60 deg underside tilt and crop) so 0:00 matches. South America and Africa tapers fill the lower-middle third, large and glowing orange; India secondary. Three thick white drip-arrows from Cape Froward, Cape Agulhas and Kanyakumari run into a yellow #FFD23F ring at bottom centre with a white '?' inside (the unresolved question). Atmosphere and night lights off for 120-px legibility. Pair with title 1 or 3.

POINTING AT WHAT? (WHAT in red). Same frame-1 render; the three drip-arrows stop at the edge of the yellow ring and the white '?' inside it is enlarged. The title says 'south'; the thumbnail opens the deeper gap the video pays off at s074 and s079-s081 (they point back to Antarctica). Pair with title 1 or 3.

THEY POINT HERE (HERE in red; deliberately not 'ALL'). Same frame-1 render plus dotted ghost outlines of South America, Africa and India snapped into the yellow ring (the s007 one-second flash frame) and one fat white arrow aimed at the ring. No Australia slab (Australia's Cape York points north, s091). Shows the shape of the answer without explaining it. Pair with title 1. Test all three with Test & Compare on title 1, judged on watch-time share; check at 120 px next to RealLifeLore / Johnny Harris. Optional 4th (story) arm, only with title 4: same globe, torn sepia strip top-right, '"NOT AN ACCIDENT"' in quote marks with a small 1620 tag (matches the s106 ending line).

chapters.title: Why does Earth look like it's dripping?
Why did geologists laugh at Wegener?
Where is the drip going next?

segments.text: Spin a globe, and Earth looks like it's {m:melt}melting.
segments.visual: FRAME 1 = THUMBNAIL IN MOTION (same render as thumbnail T1). globeShot keys {lat:-30, lon:20, alt:3.0, tilt:0, heading:0}, drift 2 deg/s; look {desat:0.3, dim:0.35, ovAlpha:1}; ocean navy #0A1A2E. One fillEquirect overlay: South America, Africa, India in #FF5A36, glow 24. A #FFD23F ring with a white '?' inside pulses on the South Pole (1.2 s period). At {m:melt}: three `arcs` draw on (1.0 s each, staggered 0.15 s, white, lift 0.08, headDot) from Cape Froward (-53.9,-71.3), Cape Agulhas (-34.8,20.0) and Kanyakumari (8.1,77.5) to (-78,20); then the three glows fade back to 30% over 0.3 s so s002 can re-light them.
segments.music: Cold open: pulsing low synth bed, tense and minimal, starts on frame 1.

segments.text: {m:sam}South America. {m:afr}Africa. {m:ind}India.
segments.visual: No camera travel (s001 view holds). On each marker the named landmass snaps back to full orange and a white outline of its southern tip draws on (strokeProjected, 0.35 s): {m:sam} Cape Froward, {m:afr} Cape Agulhas (NOT the Cape of Good Hope), {m:ind} Kanyakumari. No labels needed.

segments.text: {m:grl}Greenland. {m:fla}Florida. {m:baja}Baja. {m:kam}Kamchatka.
segments.visual: Hard cut on {m:grl} (6-frame whoosh) to the EQUAL EARTH FLAT MAP (new mode: one precomputed still, inverse-projected from tex/day_8k.jpg, 30% desat, navy ocean, faint graticule; markers placed with the forward Equal Earth formula). South America, Africa and India are already orange. Each tip fills orange with a white outline on its word: Cape Farewell 59.8N 43.9W; Cape Sable 25.3N 81.1W and Cabo San Lucas 22.9N 109.9W (tips_admin1); Cape Lopatka 50.9N 156.7E (tips_admin1 Kamchatka). One pill at a time, each fading as the next pops. TTS: check 'Baja' (BAH-hah) and 'Kamchatka' (kam-CHAHT-kuh) before lock; alias in TTS input only.

segments.text: Every point aims {m:south}south. Like somebody left the planet on the dashboard in {m:july}July.
segments.visual: Flat map holds. At {m:south}: all seven tips get a short #FFD23F drip arrow pointing straight down (len 70 px, staggered 0.06 s). At {m:july}: hard cut to EXPLORER GAG 1 (~3 s, separate stage): tinyPlanet radius 3, rotated so Cape Agulhas sits just in front of the top point, warm 2D sun flare top-right. An orange 3D teardrop (sphere + cone, 0.25 units) swells at the cape and slides down the planet's front curve. The Explorer walks to the edge (Walk 0.4 s), reaches down to catch it (Interact 1.0 s); the drop slips past his fingers and falls off into space; he wobbles at the edge (HitRecieve_2). Cut on the wobble into s005.
segments.humor: Narration: the planet left on the dashboard in July (melting-crayon image). EXPLORER GAG 1: tries to catch the drip and nearly falls off Africa (Walk, Interact, HitRecieve_2).
sfx: cartoon_fall (-10) on the wobble (the only fall whistle in the video)

segments.text: {m:twothirds}Two-thirds of all land is north of the {m:eq}equator. So are nearly {m:nine}nine in ten of us.
segments.visual: Photoreal globe {lat:15, lon:20, alt:3.2}. At {m:twothirds}: setOverlayURL('tex/data/land_north.png') fades in orange while look.dim rises to 0.45 (southern land darkens). At {m:eq}: a glowing white equator ring draws on (1.0 s) and a two-part split bar (right third, above the bottom 12%) fills to the two-thirds mark, no digits. At {m:nine}: land overlay drops to 30%; white dots for every city in ne_110m_populated_places_simple pop in (radius proportional to sqrt(pop_max)), heavily northern; the bar refills to the nine-in-ten mark.

segments.text: You've probably heard those southern points are just a {m:coin}coincidence.
segments.visual: Globe keeps drifting. At {m:coin}: a 2D gold coin spins up in front of the globe (scaleX oscillation, 1.5 turns/s). Generic coin only: no channel names, no thumbnails of other videos.

segments.text: They're {m:not}not. Not {m:entirely}entirely.
segments.visual: Music cut 0.5 s before 'They're'. At {m:not}: the coin freezes and cracks in two. At {m:entirely}: a 1.0 s UNEXPLAINED flash of the final answer: paleo globe from a south-polar camera (paleo/coast_180.json) with South America, Africa and India clamped around Antarctica's yellow ring, then snap back to today's tilted globe.
segments.music: Bed returns heavier after the cut.

segments.text: So {m:why}why do the continents point south? By the end, you'll know what they're really {m:pointing}pointing at.
segments.visual: Slow push-in on the s001 tilted globe; the three drip arcs redraw and converge on Antarctica's ring with the white '?'. Kinetic headline (F.headline) lands on the question. At {m:pointing} the ring flares. SHORTS CUT ends here; for the Short replace the second sentence with 'The full story is on the channel.' MARKER CUES: {m:why} the kinetic headline starts rising word by word.
onscreen: WHY DO THE CONTINENTS POINT SOUTH?

segments.text: Along the way: why you can't dig to China from {m:usa}anywhere in America.
segments.visual: Teaser, nothing explained. At {m:usa}: 1.8 s hard cut to the cutawayEarth stage, shell rotated so Kansas is on top (setFromUnitVectors(llDir(39.83,-98.58), up)); drillDir grows the cyan line from the top through the core and out the bottom in 1.2 s; a yellow '?' pops at the exit. Camera st.lookFrom([6,3.5,6],[0,0.3,0],32).

segments.text: A theory from {m:t1875}eighteen seventy-five that explained all of it, and was {m:wrong}dead wrong. And {m:last}the last one: the four continents your country might {m:crash}crash into. Eventually.
segments.visual: At {m:t1875}: 0.8 s sepia flash of Green's Figure 5 (assets/pd/green_fig45.jpg, lower half), then the tetraEarth stage with k 0->1 over 1.5 s (yellow edges). At {m:wrong}: it snaps back to a sphere (k 1->0, E.outBack) under a red X stamp. At {m:last}: cut to the cold-open globe spinning forward fast. At {m:crash}: 1.0 s flash of the 2x2 grid of the four model end-state stills (pre-rendered in s099-s102), the white US marker pulsing in every tile; no single neighbor is shown. Hard cut to black on 'Eventually'.
segments.humor: 'Eventually.' undercuts the doom.
sfx: impact_deep (-6) on the cut to black

segments.text: Bad news: you're not the first to notice. {m:bacon}Not even close.
segments.visual: From black, fade up on the s003 Equal Earth flat map with the seven orange tips. A sepia paper wash wipes left to right across it (sepia grade, grain 10) while a year counter top-left (JetBrains Mono) rolls back 2026 -> 1620. At {m:bacon}: cross-dissolve to the 1620 Instauratio Magna engraved title page (assets/pd/title_1620.jpg) in a rounded print frame; Ken Burns from the galleon (cx 0.5, cy 0.75, zoom 1.6) up to the title (0.5, 0.3, 1.15).
segments.humor: Self-aware 'bad news' for the viewer.
segments.music: Switch to felt piano + soft strings for the history.

segments.text: In sixteen twenty, Francis {m:fb}Bacon wrote that the Old World and the New are both {m:narrow}'narrow and pointed toward the south.'
segments.visual: At {m:fb}: Ken Burns on Bacon's portrait (assets/pd/bacon.jpg, Paul van Somer 1617, sepia print frame). At {m:narrow}: cut to the 1620 page that actually holds the passage: archive.org instauratiomagna00baco leaf n246 = printed p.239 (research/script/visual-director/dl_ia/n246.jpg; NOT assets/pd/bacon_p232.jpg, which is p.240 and lacks it). Ken Burns into lines 4-6; an orange glowPath underline draws under 'acuminati' (normalized box x0.568 y0.229 w0.130 h0.022) and the pill swaps to the Latin gloss. Then the Parasceve page (leaf n387 = printed p.20, dl_ia/n387.jpg) slides in from the right with an underline under 'ad Austrum angusta & veluti acuminata' (x0.154 y0.334 w0.517 h0.019) and a small 'x2' stamp: he wrote it twice. Visual only, no narration.

segments.text: And in the same {m:breath}breath, he said Africa and South America's matching capes were {m:accident}'not to be attributed to mere accident.'
segments.visual: 0-2.3 s: globe {lat:-25, lon:-10, alt:2.6}, Africa and South America outlined white side by side, their southern capes pulsing orange. At {m:breath}: back to page n246 and tilt the Ken Burns UP two lines from 'acuminati' (it is literally the sentence above, on the same 1620 page). At {m:accident}: orange underlines draw under 'quod non temere ac-' (x0.553 y0.131 w0.276 h0.017) and 'cidit.' (x0.079 y0.153 w0.064 h0.016); the English pill fades in. This proves thumbnail/title wording by ~1:05.
onscreen: "NOT TO BE ATTRIBUTED TO MERE ACCIDENT"
segments.music: Soft piano accent on 'accident'.

segments.text: Then he wrote down an open question: is there even a {m:southcont}southern continent down there? Nobody would lay eyes on {m:antar}Antarctica for two more {m:cent}centuries. Remember {m:rem}that.
segments.visual: Camera dives to the bottom of the globe at {m:southcont}; Antarctica is hidden under a soft white fog (white Antarctica polygon in the overlay canvas, feathered) with a hand-lettered '?'. A sepia year ticker flicks 1620 -> 1820 and the fog thins; freeze-drift on the '?' (drift keeps it alive). MARKER CUES: {m:antar} the sepia ticker starts 1620 -> 1820; {m:cent} the fog thins; {m:rem} hold-drift on the '?'.

segments.text: Now, you may have heard that Bacon predicted continental drift. {m:scratch}He didn't.
segments.visual: Globe {lat:-15, lon:-15, alt:2.4}: South America's rings drag (moves, true size) toward Africa and rotate to snap into its coast. At {m:scratch}: frozen mid-snap, a red JUICE CHECK: FALSE stamp slams down (brand verdict device, first use).
segments.humor: Record-scratch myth-bust.

segments.text: He wasn't {m:snap}snapping Africa and South America together like puzzle pieces. He was saying they're shaped {m:same}alike, side by side.
segments.visual: The jigsaw rewinds (South America slides back home). At {m:same}: both continents sit side by side in today's orientation; a white isosceles taper triangle draws over each, same orientation, with an approx-equals sign between them. MARKER CUES: {m:snap} the jigsaw rewind starts.

segments.text: So Bacon saw the drip, but never tried to {m:explain}explain it. For centuries, nobody else {m:anyone}could. That did not stop them from {m:try}trying.
segments.visual: Page n246 shrinks into a print frame top-left over the slowly turning drip globe. At {m:explain}: a big '?' draws on Antarctica's ring. At {m:anyone}: archival pages drop onto a stack, one every 1.1 s: Forster 1778 p.13 (fetch archive.org b30408623 page 13), Green 1875 preface (vestigesmolteng00greegoog leaf n7), Guyot 1849 p.22 (fetch earthmanlectures00guyo page 22). At {m:try}: the pile overflows the frame and topples off sideways.
segments.humor: Dry understatement: 'That did not stop them from trying.'

segments.text: Captain {m:cook}Cook's naturalist, Johann Reinhold Forster, claimed that every great southern tip looks {m:alike}alike: high, rocky, the end of a {m:mtn}mountain chain.
segments.visual: 0-2.6 s: Ken Burns on assets/pd/forster.png (Bause after Graff) in a sepia print frame. At {m:alike}: cut to the globe, relief 1.0, patch tex/patch/s_america_tip.jpg, camera low over Cape Froward looking north up the Andes {lat:-52, lon:-72, alt:0.25, tilt:55, heading:0}. At {m:mtn}: whip to Kanyakumari (patch s_india.jpg, tilt 55) looking north up the Western Ghats. Show only real terrain; draw NO 'mountain chain' lines from Cape Agulhas or Tasmania (Forster's rule is his claim, not ours). MARKER CUES: {m:cook} the Forster portrait Ken Burns starts.

segments.text: His {m:expl}explanation? A giant flood came {m:wave}roaring in from the south-west and {m:carved}carved every one of them. Some of the top scientists of the day {m:bought}bought it. Geology later asked for a {m:refund}refund.
segments.visual: On 'His explanation?': the fetched Forster 1778 p.13 scan, orange underline under 'a violent flood coming from the south-west'. At {m:wave}: cut to EXPLORER GAG 2 and stay there: tiny planet with the South Atlantic facing camera; a flat stylised 2D wave (cyan crest, white foam line) sweeps from lower-left (south-west) to upper-right over 1.4 s. The Explorer runs (Run_Right) but too late; the crest clips him (HitRecieve); it passes, and he stands soaked (Idle_Neutral) while a drop falls off his beard (now he's the one dripping). At {m:bought}: a small sepia wax seal stamps onto the wave graphic. At {m:refund}: the wave deflates like a pool float (scaleY 1 -> 0.1, 0.4 s). MARKER CUES: {m:expl} the Forster p.13 underline draws; {m:carved} the crest clips the Explorer (HitRecieve).
segments.humor: EXPLORER GAG 2: soaked by Forster's imaginary flood (Run_Right, HitRecieve, Idle_Neutral). Tag: 'Geology later asked for a refund.'

segments.text: By the eighteen-forties, the most famous scientist alive was calling the tips {m:pyr}'pyramidal.' And someone had written down almost the exact {m:list}list you saw at the start.
segments.visual: 2.5 s Ken Burns on Humboldt's portrait (Stieler 1843, PD; fetch from Commons) in a sepia frame. At {m:pyr}: cut to the s001 tilted globe; thin white triangle outlines snap onto the southern ends of South America, Africa and India (plants the pyramid for Chapter 3). At {m:list}: Ken Burns on the fetched Guyot 1849 p.22 scan.

segments.text: {m:l1}Greenland, {m:l2}Baja, {m:l3}Florida, {m:l4}India, {m:l5}Kamchatka. 'All their points turned towards the south.'
segments.visual: Match-cut to the EXACT s003 Equal Earth framing; re-pop the five tips in the same rhythm and with the same pop_ui thump as 0:04 (callback). The quote types on last.
onscreen: "ALL THEIR POINTS TURNED TOWARDS THE SOUTH"
sfx: pop_ui (-14) x5, same as the cold open

segments.text: Then, in the {m:seventies}nineteen-seventies, the pattern got its name, as a {m:joke}joke. A magazine writer called it {m:drip}'continental drip': a fake theory you could prove just by {m:staring}staring at a map.
segments.visual: Typewriter card on cream paper (JetBrains Mono 500; generic, no real magazine branding). At {m:joke}: a coffee-stained sheet slides in. At {m:drip}: 'CONTINENTAL DRIFT' types out, then the 'FT' is struck through and a 'P' typed over it: DRIP. MARKER CUES: {m:seventies} the '1973' pill pops; {m:staring} a magnifying-glass icon sweeps across a small world-map card.
segments.humor: DRIFT gets retyped as DRIP on screen.
segments.music: Light, playful pizzicato under the joke.

segments.text: Three years later, a geologist published his own {m:version}version of the joke. Hold on to {m:hold}him. He matters more than you'd {m:think}think.
segments.visual: A second typewriter sheet slides in behind the first; its byline is blurred. At {m:hold}: a yellow ring circles the blur; slow push-in. On 'more than you'd think': a 0.5 s flicker of the Gondwana paleo still behind the paper, like a watermark (plants the Chapter 5 twist). MARKER CUES: {m:version} the second sheet slides in; {m:think} the 0.5 s Gondwana watermark flicker.

segments.text: But the shapes are just the {m:first}first clue. The next one is on the {m:far}far side of the planet.
segments.visual: At {m:first}: the seven drip arrows flash once on the cold-open globe while the camera pushes in. At {m:far}: hard cut to the cutawayEarth stage with the North Pole on top; drillDir draws the cyan line from the pole through the core and out the South Pole in 1.4 s while the camera dollies from [6,3.5,6] to [4.5,2.6,4.5] (target [0,0.3,0], fov 32).
segments.music: Riser into Chapter 2; switch to the pulsing synth + strings data bed.
